terra.problem: The text says God’s lamp shone above Job’s head, not that God was holding it.
The verse does not say whether Job was carrying his own lamp.
Papa Dorin has a gold base that stays with him, so saying he takes steps conflicts with his design.
The text says the young men withdrew. It does not describe a whole crowd making room for Job to walk through.
The text does not say nobody bowed or that everybody made room for Job.
The text says the young men withdrew, but does not say nobody ran toward Job.
The old men rose to their feet, but the text does not say they had been sitting in seats.
The explanation states what Job was proud of as a fact, though the text does not say he felt proud.
Being called blessed is changed into his blessing coming from his actions. The claim that nobody spoke about his house also goes beyond the text.
The text does not say the people Job mentions had little to give back.
“Righteousness was walking right on him” is an unclear image rather than a joke that clicks.
Job says he served as feet to the lame, but the text does not specify that he helped people get to particular places.
The text does not specify that Job helped people get where they needed to go.
“What people were missing” can imply missing body parts, which the text does not say.
“Even as a king” turns Job’s comparison into a statement that he was a king. He says he dwelt as a king.
Calling Job a man with herds brings in a fact from outside this passage without a reference.
The text does not say the bow is still there or that nobody took it. Job describes it as unstrung.
Job says his dignity is driven away as by the wind, not that wind actually drove it off.
The final sentence treats the wind as actually carrying something off, rather than keeping Job’s comparison, “as by the wind.”
Job says he wept for those in trouble, not that he came close and wept with them.
The text does not say Job’s instruments once played other songs.
“Job isn’t there yet” suggests a future victory that this passage does not state.
